description: Observed-order-of-accuracy sweep for grids/mpas/rules/fv_divergence_cell (order:1) over the icosahedral refinement family levels 0/1/2 (12/42/162 cells). Subsystem ref paths cannot be metaparameterized, so each resolution entry names its own thin problem file (problems/divergence_mpas_l{0,1,2}.esm — the rebinding recipe of problems/divergence_mpas.esm made concrete); the per-resolution `bindings` are empty because each problem file closes the grid metaparameters at its import edge. n semantics: scripts/check_convergence_order.py computes order against n ratios, so n is an effective 1-D resolution n_eff = round(1000 * sqrt(NCELLS / (4 pi))) proportional to 1/h with h = sqrt(4 pi / NCELLS), the mean cell spacing on the unit sphere (the same h the grid's cell_area_mean template encodes): NCELLS 12/42/162 -> n = 977/1828/3590, ratios 1.871/1.964 (integer rounding shifts observed orders by < 0.001). The measured error is the discrete divergence of the P2-flux fixture vs the analytic divergence -3(3 z^2 - 1) (derivation in the problem files). Expected order: the TRiSK cell divergence is guaranteed first-order on arbitrary Voronoi meshes, and the max-norm tracks exactly that here (Julia-measured pairwise Linf orders 1.00 and 0.85 across the three levels; median 0.93, asserted as 1.0 +/- 0.25 — the tolerance is wide because only two order samples exist and the 12-cell mesh is preasymptotic, per the golden). The relative-L2 error superconverges on this quasi-symmetric bisected family (pairwise orders ~1.75/1.52, between the guaranteed 1 and the centroidal-mesh 2, because the pentagon-adjacent first-order region has vanishing measure); it is recorded in the problem files' inline tolerances but deliberately NOT order-gated here — a single expected_order cannot honestly cover both norms on three meshes.
